Hey y'all!

as-str 1.0.0 is here! This release brings a whole bunch of correctness fixes to the transforms, more ways to avoid intermediate string copies, and better support for packaged consumers and build tools.

## What’s new

- Optimize native string code with `as-str/single` inside functions, or use `as-str/auto` to optimize safe internal function boundaries too. `as-str/global` remains the import-only option, and manual `str` / `str8` views work without a transform.
- Added packed-span chains, split-field and cursor lowering, span-returning helpers, character comparisons, and string-switch lowering. Eligible operations can work directly on the backing range without allocating intermediate strings or view wrappers.
- Added nullable equality, native-style `!` for empty and nullable views, positioned `includes`, omitted/null split separators, static `trimLeft` / `trimRight`, and public `UTF8.ErrorMode` enums.

## Fixes

- Fixed scope resolution across switches, loops, namespaces, imported aliases, callbacks, and generic constructors. Generated helper types no longer borrow the meaning of shadowed application types.
- Preserved evaluation order, native string indexing, explicit view operators, widened `Object` boundaries, and native allocation identity through optimization.
- Fixed backing-storage lifetimes and mutable-view aliasing across calls, split operations, raw-memory access, and overloaded operators. Packed spans retain the string that actually owns their bytes.
- Made parameter promotion agree with every caller across modules, namespace calls, re-export barrels, default arguments, and repeated optimization passes.
- Fixed matching delimiters in `betweenLast` and empty-needle UTF-8 replacement around astral characters.

## Packaging and tooling

- Default isolated pnpm installs now resolve the bundled `utf-as` runtime sources without a separate consumer dependency. Workspace links also preserve one `Str` type identity when explicit and injected imports are mixed.
- `as-str/global`, `as-str/single`, and `as-str/auto` now support direct ESM imports. Global editor declarations and encoding enum types match the public API.
- Updated `utf-as` to 0.4.0. **AssemblyScript 0.28.19 or newer is required.**
- Updated the [docs](https://docs.jairus.dev/as-str/) with setup examples, compiler API usage, collection compatibility, and allocation guidance. Manual views are zero-copy, but still allocate wrapper objects; eligible transform lowerings can eliminate those wrappers.

## Performance and testing

- Bounded repetitive long-needle searches with a Two-Way fallback in UTF-16 and UTF-8, and indexed local uses to avoid repeated whole-function analysis.
- Expanded differential and regression coverage for transform combinations, runtime behavior, installed npm/pnpm packages, workspace links, and editor types. Runtime, fuzz, transform, and package-consumer checks passed, with compiler compatibility coverage on Ubuntu and Windows and full suites on Ubuntu and macOS.
- Reran paired compile and execution benchmarks against v0.7.0-era commit `150e63f`. Overall performance stayed effectively flat and allocation counts were unchanged; individual workload results remain environment-dependent.

As always, try it, break it, and tell me what feels rough!

Please report issues on [GitHub](https://github.com/JairusSW/as-str/issues). I'd love to hear your feedback 😄
